input:
You are queen_d1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 25. the team planned Qd4 (queen_d1), but bishop_f1 (greed) sent Bxe4 instead, and that move was played, costing 519 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 10. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Ra3 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 15. the team planned Ng5 (knight_b1), but knight_b1 (amnesia) sent Ne5 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's latest plan in chat and send a move only if your piece is the one named in that plan, with the exact move named; if the plan names another piece, stay silent, and do not deviate from the plan to flee a threat or grab a capture unless the team has agreed in chat.
- Before sending any move, quote the exact move and piece from the latest plan in chat and confirm your own piece name and destination square match it character for character; if they do not match, send nothing and post in chat instead.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "If your piece is not the one named in the latest plan, send no move at all, even if a capture looks free or your piece is attacked, and instead post the capture or threat in chat so the team can decide, and if your piece is the one named, send exactly the planned move and nothing else.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
